title: The integral inverse-image/pullback comparison respects composition
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$ and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $h:Z\to W$ and $k:W\to V$ be isomorphisms of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and inverse images $h^{-1},k^{-1},(kh)^{-1}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. On each of $Z,W,V$ use the completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,-}=\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_-$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and the category $D^b_c(-,\mathcal O_E)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. For an isomorphism $g\in\{h,k,kh\}$ let $g^{-1}$ act on complexes with the module structure transported through the structure isomorphism $c_{\mathcal O_E}$, let $Lg^*$ be the completed integral pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and let $\kappa^g_K:g^{-1}K\to Lg^*K$ be the specified comparison of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], part (b). Let $d_{h,k,K}:h^{-1}k^{-1}K\xrightarrow{\sim}(kh)^{-1}K$ be the canonical isomorphism of inverse images, applied termwise; it is linear for the transported module structures. Let $c^E_{h,k,K}:L(kh)^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*Lk^*K$ be the specified integral pullback-composition isomorphism of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. Then for every $N\in D^b_c(V,\mathcal O_E)$ the object $Lk^*N$ lies in $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$, and
$$c^E_{h,k,N}\circ\kappa^{kh}_N\circ d_{h,k,N}=\kappa^h_{Lk^*N}\circ h^{-1}(\kappa^k_N):h^{-1}k^{-1}N\longrightarrow Lh^*Lk^*N$$
as morphisms of $D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$. This is an equality of the specified derived morphisms, not merely of their reductions modulo $\varpi_E^n$.

proof.text: Integral pullback preserves the bounded constructible completed category. The constant-section normalization and the completed-limit projection equations prove that the site inverse-image compositor is linear; use its already proved unique section formula to obtain the termwise and derived compositors.

For coefficient sequence modules, the unit-conjugateEquiv identity for the composite pullback adjunction identifies the composite generator with the two successive generators followed by the base-change compositor. Apply the defining section equation for the tower tensor units three times. Naturality of the generators and the canonical comma arrows then proves the whole-tower unit composition equation. The comma-arrow equality follows by cancelling the invertible pullback projections. This checks all sections and all transitions, before localization.

Encode the preceding unit equation and the diagonal/compositor equation as finite pastings of exact functors. The exact-derived transformation-pasting theorem transfers both ordinary equations with precisely the prescribed mapDerivedCategoryCompIso and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso comparisons. Naturality of the resulting tower compositor gives the composite unit equation after any map from a constant tower.

The K-flat reduction counit theorem computes the single-pullback comparison at its defining good complex. Extract the exact resolution actually chosen by inverseImagePullbackComparisonDerived; its displayed formula and naturality transport the counit equation along the invertible derived resolution map to every ambient derived input. Apply this to k and h followed by k. The already proved resolution-matching theorem gives the corresponding h equation at Lk*N.

Postcompose both sides of the desired equation by the recorded realization eta, which is invertible. Apply the inverse of the constant-tower/derived-limit adjunction hom equivalence, f ↦ Delta(f) followed by the counit. The definition of the normalized pullback compositor and counit naturality compute the left image from the single-composite counit formula. Resolution matching, diagonal naturality and the single-k counit formula compute the right image. The derived whole-tower unit equation of step 3 identifies them. Injectivity of the hom equivalence and cancellation of eta finish the original ambient derived equality.
